title: Rabbi Pedat the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Tikkunei Zohar 29](https://www.sefaria.org/Tikkunei_Zohar.100a.5), and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said of him that he is a completely righteous man.
Iggeret Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, beginning of chapter 2, likewise mentions Rabbi Pedat the earlier, of the generation before Rabbi.
Yuchasin presents Rabbi Pedat as a colleague of Rabbi who lived a long life. Its reading of Moed Katan 25b was: “When Rabbi Pedat died, his grandson Rabbi Pedat eulogized him.”[^3]

notes.text: The long-lived Pedat, Rabbi’s colleague, and the same-named grandson are Hyman’s claims. His reported Yuchasin reading is preserved without merging it with other Pedat entries.

In the linked [Tikkunei Zohar 100a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tikkunei_Zohar.100a.5), Rabbi Elazar calls Rabbi Pedat completely righteous. The link leads to that statement, and the translation retains Hyman’s locator “29.” Its numbering scheme and the reported Iggeret and Yuchasin readings remain unverified.

Heilprin expressly cites Yuchasin for the elder Pedat, a colleague of Rabbi, and a grandson also named Pedat. The linked Talmud passage has Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar eulogizing Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman’s reported Yuchasin version of the eulogy remains unverified. See [Moed Katan 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25b.10). See [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2937&lang=en).
